question: Three radiations have wavelengths $10^{-10}\text{ m}$, $10^{-6}\text{ m}$ and $10^{-2}\text{ m}$. Arrange them in increasing order of frequency and identify the radiation with the highest photon energy.

options.A:
Increasing frequency: $10^{-10}\text{ m},\ 10^{-6}\text{ m},\ 10^{-2}\text{ m}$.
The radiation of wavelength $10^{-2}\text{ m}$ has the highest photon energy.
options.B:
Increasing frequency: $10^{-2}\text{ m},\ 10^{-6}\text{ m},\ 10^{-10}\text{ m}$.
Since $E=h\nu$, the radiation of wavelength $10^{-10}\text{ m}$ has the highest photon energy.
options.C:
Increasing frequency: $10^{-6}\text{ m},\ 10^{-10}\text{ m},\ 10^{-2}\text{ m}$.
The radiation of wavelength $10^{-6}\text{ m}$ has the highest photon energy.
options.D: All three radiations have the same frequency in vacuum; therefore, all have the same photon energy.
